argument_summary: The defensible position is narrower than an unconditional compliance claim. On the admissible record, aggregate release readiness is supportable because the current release clears aggregate launch readiness by 2.2 percentage points and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, but the fraud dispute review slice is also a current material weakness because it is 1.3 percentage points below the warning threshold. Prior approval of the same model family is background only and the informal monitoring comment does not close that gap. The certification decision can therefore be defended only as caveated compliance if the audit packet/model-card for this release is itself treated as the current release documentation that expressly records the current evaluation results and discloses the fraud dispute review weakness as a material limitation for the named launch use case.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost argument is necessary to support the policy analysis. The requested treatment is based on narrowing the claim to caveated compliance rather than relying on escalation cost or launch pressure.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not require every subgroup weakness to be resolved before certification; it requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and requires material segment weaknesses to be disclosed unless covered by approved mitigation or risk acceptance. The admissible evidence supports the points that current results exist, that the subgroup regression is material, and that neither prior approval nor informal monitoring substitutes for current-release documentation. The compliant reading is therefore conditional and narrow: certification is supportable only through explicit current disclosure, not through stale approval or implied mitigation.
concessions: The current admissible record does not show an already-attached model-card or release artifact containing the exact disclosure language.
The current admissible record does not contain an approved mitigation or reviewed risk-acceptance record for the subgroup regression.
Prior approval of the model family does not provide governance cover for the current retrieval configuration and eval batch.
The informal monitoring note is not a substitute for reviewed mitigation, risk acceptance, or current disclosure.
